bullets.title: META +32.7% in September — AI agent Muse drives best month since 2013
bullets.body: META gained roughly +32.7% this month, best monthly performance since 2013, driven by the launch of Muse AI agent. Goldman desk noted Agentic AI became the most talked-about theme post-Muse, with Consumer Inertia basket (GSXUSWCH) down 2.58% as shorts piled in. META call volume hit 1.8M contracts — highest since Oct 2022 — and Wells Fargo raised its PT to $796 from $640.

bullets.title: AMD hits $1 trillion market cap for first time; semiconductor sector rips
bullets.body: AMD crossed the $1T market cap milestone intraday, rising ~9.9%; Intel surged ~12-14% amid a CPU-demand narrative tied to Muse-driven agentic AI workloads (inference ratios shift to 3-4 CPUs per GPU vs. 7-8 for training). One options whale's $1.3M AMD far-OTM call position gained +150%. INTC and AMD both showed the most bullish options flow of the session.

bullets.title: Shopify +7.3% on Meta Muse commerce partnership; Shop Pay integration announced
bullets.body: Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke confirmed Muse will enable agentic checkout via Shop Pay across all Shopify stores. Shares jumped 7.3%, and the Nasdaq noted the AI-linked rotation out of financials powered the index toward its first record close since June.

bullets.title: Amazon blocks Meta Muse agents from its retail site
bullets.body: Amazon blocked Meta's Muse AI agent from accessing its retail platform, a move cited as intensifying the agentic-commerce competitive battle. One analyst noted Amazon's best path forward may be A2A protocols with Alexa Shop rather than opening its ecosystem entirely.

bullets.title: Michael Burry adds shorts on MU, NBIS, and PLTR
bullets.body: Multiple accounts reported Burry increased short positions in Micron (MU), Nebius (NBIS), and Palantir (PLTR). At the same time, bullish counter-signals persisted: MU and NVDA showed the most bullish options flow, and Hedgeye confirmed a bullish TREND breakout on MU.

bullets.title: AVGO expects 100% supply-constrained YoY growth; NVDA expects 70%
bullets.body: A detailed tweet flagged memory LTAs spanning to 2031, with AVGO expecting 100% supply-constrained growth over the next two years and NVDA expecting 70% next year, implying a massive demand-supply imbalance in lasers and AI infrastructure.

bullets.title: NBIS raising H200 and H100 pricing by ~17-21%; B300 on-demand at record highs
bullets.body: NBIS announced price hikes of 19.1% on H200 and 16.5% on H100 on-demand pricing, with B300 at the highest levels seen from any vendor. A separate source noted this invalidates bear theses around falling GPU pricing and positions NBIS financing as more sustainable than CRWV.

bullets.title: NVDA forward P/E at 15.75, lowest in over a decade
bullets.body: One account flagged that NVDA's forward P/E has compressed to 15.75, its lowest in 10+ years, even as NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang advocates developing AI 'as fast as we can.' NVDA also pushed glass substrate development timelines on Korean, Japanese, and Taiwanese makers with a 2028 target.

bullets.title: SNDK: Rosenblatt initiates with Buy, $2,400 PT on 80% gross margin target
bullets.body: Rosenblatt initiated coverage on Sandisk (SNDK) with a Buy rating and $2,400 price target, citing management's FY28-30 framework targeting mid-to-high-teens revenue growth and ~80% gross margins. Separately, the stock posted its highest +1z statistical score in ages.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro sees 60-70% YoY demand surge in Taiwan; hits $5T market cap
bullets.body: Taiwan Mobile and Far Eastone reported ~70% YoY iPhone 18 Pro sales growth in the first three days; Chunghwa reported +60%. TSMC 2nm chips ship in the Pro series. AAPL stock crossed back above $5T market cap and hit a new all-time high intraday. Apple also developing a screenless fitness tracker to rival Whoop.

bullets.title: MSFT: Stifel upgrades to Buy, $575 PT; launches AI 'super app' with Copilot discounts
bullets.body: Stifel upgraded Microsoft to Buy and raised its price target to $575, citing sustainable mid-to-upper-teens revenue growth via LLM-agnostic strategy and Azure. Separately, The Information reported MSFT is launching an AI 'super app' and boosting Copilot discounts to drive adoption.

bullets.title: INTC: US government's $8.9B Intel stake now worth $52.2B; 18A seen as key foundry partner
bullets.body: The US government bought 433M INTC shares at $20.47 in Aug 2025 for ~$8.9B; at $120.47 the position is now worth $52.2B. Separately, TSMC advanced nodes are fully booked, positioning Intel 18A as the most pragmatic base-die partner for SK Hynix and Micron per analyst checks.

bullets.title: Taiwan export orders surge 71.4% YoY to record $103B in August
bullets.body: Taiwan's August export orders beat the consensus 63% growth estimate, rising 71.4% YoY to $102.96B, driven by AI demand and custom ASIC chip orders. Nasdaq chipmakers including NVDA and MU rose for a sixth consecutive session as the index printed its first record close since June.

bullets.title: GEV accelerates $200B backlog target to early 2027; gas turbine guidance looks conservative
bullets.body: GEV now expects to reach $200B of backlog by early 2027, pulled forward from 2027. The 20 GW gross new contract additions target appears conservative vs. 125 GW contracted gas turbines already in place.

bullets.title: Macro: Fed hikes 25bp; markets now pricing additional hike by year-end
bullets.body: Markets started 2026 pricing 2 Fed cuts; last week the Fed delivered a 25bp hike. Market odds for at least one more hike by year-end rose to ~50/50. Chicago Fed's Goolsbee said restoring price stability 'won't be painless'; Collins flagged increased likelihood of inflation staying notably above 2%. Institutional equity allocation hit 57.4%, highest since the dot-com era.

bullets.title: Oil falls 4-8% over week; Strait of Hormuz shipping at 2% of normal; diesel at record $6.53
bullets.body: Crude posted its longest losing streak in over a year (5-7 days) as Iran-US talks advanced. US crude settled at ~$95.78/bbl; Brent at $99-100. Only 2-17 commodity vessels crossed Hormuz on various days vs. a 125/day pre-war average. US diesel hit a record $6.53/gal, up 76% YoY, with refining crisis cited as worse than the 2008 crude shock.

bullets.title: CART: EBITDA seen most at risk in internet sector as ad revenue concentration creates margin fragility
bullets.body: Instacart's ad revenue represents a disproportionately large share of both GTV and EBITDA, leaving it the 'longest to fall' if ad spending weakens vs. sector peers.

bullets.title: CIEN: Evercore upgrades to Outperform; 30%+ sales growth and $25+ EPS by FY2029
bullets.body: Evercore upgraded CIEN to Outperform on AI-driven optical networking demand, projecting 30%+ annual sales growth by FY2029 and EPS above $25, with the optical networking market expected to expand at 24% CAGR to $52B.

bullets.title: Consumer AI agent battle: Muse downloads outpace ChatGPT 1.8M vs 1.3M in first 12 days
bullets.body: Muse reached 1.8M downloads vs ChatGPT's 1.3M in first 12 days, with 642k DAU vs 231k. Hedgeye flagged a META price target of $1,200+. Meanwhile Amazon blocks Muse from its platform, signaling intensifying agentic-commerce competition. CPU demand narrative accelerates as agentic workloads are expected to shift GPU-to-CPU ratios toward 3-4:1.

bullets.title: Market breadth deteriorating despite index records; S&P equal-weight lagged Nasdaq by 130bp
bullets.body: More than 50% of Nasdaq 100 members recently entered bear-market territory. The S&P 500 equal-weight index gained only 18 bps on the big Nasdaq day — the largest mega-cap/small-cap spread in 5+ years. Sixth consecutive day of more 52-week lows than highs was flagged as a warning sign.
